[Problem on LeetCode](https://leetcode.com/problems/triangle-judgement/)

## Problem

Each row of `Triangle` holds three positive lengths `x`, `y`, `z`. For every row, report whether the three segments can form a triangle (`'Yes'` or `'No'`).

## Formalisation

This is not a selection: every row is kept. Instead each tuple is extended by a computed value, a generalised projection

$$
\pi_{\,x,\,y,\,z,\,\chi(x,y,z)}(T), \qquad
\chi(x,y,z) =
\begin{cases}
\text{Yes}, & x + y > z \ \wedge\ x + z > y \ \wedge\ y + z > x, \\
\text{No}, & \text{otherwise.}
\end{cases}
$$

The three inequalities collapse to one. Without loss of generality let $z = \max(x,y,z)$. Then $x + z > z \ge y$ and $y + z > z \ge x$ (all lengths are positive), so the second and third inequalities hold automatically and only $x + y > z$ can fail. Hence

$$
\chi(x,y,z) = \text{Yes} \iff x + y + z > 2\max(x,y,z).
$$

This also explains my first attempt: testing only $x + y > z$ is correct exactly when $z$ happens to be the longest side.

## Solution

```sql
SELECT x, y, z,
  CASE
    WHEN x + y > z AND x + z > y AND y + z > x THEN 'Yes'
    ELSE 'No'
  END AS triangle
FROM Triangle;
```

The single-test version from the formalisation:

```sql
SELECT x, y, z,
  CASE WHEN x + y + z > 2 * GREATEST(x, y, z) THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS triangle
FROM Triangle;
```

## Pitfalls

- **Check all three inequalities, not one.** My first version treated `z` as the special side and tested only `x + y <= z`, which passes whenever `z` is the longest side and fails otherwise (8 of 11 tests passed).
- **The inequality is strict.** If $x + y = z$ the "triangle" is flat (degenerate), so the answer is `'No'`.
- **`ABS` is unnecessary.** The values are lengths, so they are positive.
- **`GREATEST` is not `MAX`.** `GREATEST(x, y, z)` takes the largest of several values in one row; `MAX(col)` is an aggregate over many rows.
- **`CASE` builds a column; `WHERE` removes rows.** Here every row must appear in the output, so the condition goes in a `CASE`, not a `WHERE`.
